cases.title: Input allocation versus table qualification and row recipe

claim.summary: The individual ordinary-C repair is exact, reviewed, landed, and window-gated at an admissible stock CDK cell. It makes no historical-release or family-transfer claim.

identity.value: dungeon row func_81811388, true symbol func_80026388, file offset 0x1831388, 56 retail bytes

recipe.value: 2.7.2-cdk, no extra compiler flags, default assembler flags
recipe.basis: ordinary candidate and existing pinned text are both exact at this stock cell, satisfying the established cell-switch rule; historical release within the split-address family is unresolved

causal.question: Why does erasing the input binding fail for the inherited volatile source at plain 2.7.2 while ordinary source matches retail at CDK?
causal.prediction: CDK will split the ordinary relocatable array address into high/lo_sum RTL before allocation and reproduce the retail registers; plain 2.7.2 will retain a different symbolic-load shape and miss.

evidence.summary: Four explicit scalar-return repairs at fixed 2.7.2 all scored distance 5: they corrected the real three-caller return contract but left the input register colouring wrong.

bounds.tested: four reasoned return forms, eight full verifiers across the two void/scalar definitions; this row's best result was 14/14 words at distance 5
bounds.untested: table qualification, alternate natural stock cells, allocator pass inputs, and source/recipe attribution controls

evidence.summary: The final ordinary returning function directly loads D_800294F8[lookup_index] and is 14/14 exact at stock 2.7.2-cdk; the non-returning plain-load form is also exact at 2.8.0, 2.8.1, and 2.95.2. Historical release provenance remains qualified.

candidate.source_change: replace the pinned void wrapper with an ordinary s32 return of func_80049DE8(target, input_value, D_800294F8[lookup_index])
candidate.result: 14/14 retail words exact; independent landing dry run passed
candidate.remaining_question: historical release provenance and any family transfer; the exact wrapper has no release-discriminating byte signature

evidence.summary: At plain 2.7.2, pin erasure leaves a five-word register mismatch and ordinary C gives 13/14 words, total 6. At CDK, both ordinary returning C and the existing pinned text are exact, so the candidate satisfies the established cell-switch control rather than a new acceptance shortcut.

Plain 2.7.2 gives the short-lived table-address quantity priority 10000 and v0 before the saved input quantity at priority 2000. CDK splits the global address into high/lo_sum RTL before allocation and ordinary source receives the retail registers.
The table is ordinary RAM with one relocatable byte load; helper func_80049DE8 is defined as integer-returning, and all three identified same-image callers consume s32 with unchanged argument types.
The ordinary candidate landed exact through apply_candidates --cells at 2.7.2-cdk, changing the source from the recorded baseline hash to the candidate hash.
The affected dungeon_deep_t8_1830 window matches in the latest gate record.
The latest SLUS SHA-1 gate matches after the exemplar landing.
The post-gate census is 6102 pins in 1283 pinned rows.

The reviewed round-39 split-address cohort found no independent exact positive. Its closest zero-pin transfer reaches total 2, and the ownership/safety controls reject a blanket de-volatile/de-pin rule, so the exemplar alone does not establish a family repair.

bounds.tested: the round-39 callback-table, direct-table, absolute-address, arithmetic-colouring, and bounds-table source forms across their recorded relevant stock cells
bounds.untested: different source reconstructions or recipes, including the separately tracked round-40 whole-struct candidate for town/func_80878974, and future rows with the same single ordinary-symbol, short-lived split-address quantity and independently proven volatile safety

evidence.summary: A separate round-40 town/func_80878974 repair uses a whole 52-byte struct copy with ASPSX 2.40, is zero-pin and byte-exact, has landed, and passed semantic review. Its publication gate is still running, so it is not yet resolved; its distinct record-copy mechanism is not an independent positive transfer control for this round-39 split-address case.

claim.summary: Selective vertex3 pointer/y lifetime splitting materially improves the fully depinned row while preserving retail length and frame, but the 33-point allocator, colouring, and scheduling residue remains non-exact.

identity.value: dungeon row func_8180B064, true symbol func_80026864, file offset 0x182b064, 1720 retail bytes

causal.question: Which ordinary lifetime, reuse, or preference makes the cell induction pseudo outrank the vertex-base pseudo while preserving the exact post-terrain region, and do the four local scheduling indels then resolve with that hard-register assignment?
causal.prediction: A source relationship grounded in the original owner or a sibling will lower vertex-base priority below 6428, raise cell-pointer priority above 6846, or create a relevant preference without perturbing words 295-429; with the retail s4/s5 assignment restored, the remaining local scheduling difference can be tested as a potentially co-adapted effect.

evidence.summary: A prior foldload probe for vert0_y compiled and changed this row, but the saved campaign record does not establish a byte-exact repair or whole-region cause.

Removing the height keep and spelling the subtraction as one signed expression gives total 4 with all 430 words present; the remaining difference is reorder-only because vert3 y work moves ahead of height completion.

bounds.tested: one signed compound height expression at fixed 2.7.2-cdk -G0, plus the supplied single-statement scheduling negatives
bounds.untested: a complete typed reconstruction of the vertex/height region and its coupled far allocation sites

evidence.summary: The current source aliases vertex pointers, packed coordinates, and y values across long live ranges; the near scheduler symptom sits inside the same region as several coupled colouring pins.

Erasing all six pins without reshaping the C yields all 430 retail words and the exact 0x80 frame/save set at 2.7.2-cdk -G0, but scores total 55. The remaining connected owners are the s4/s5 vertex/cell allocation and the vertex expression region.

bounds.tested: fully depinned inherited C at the recorded recipe plus all recognized stock cells; CDK total 55 is the best tested natural-source cell
bounds.untested: ordinary lifetime/reuse reconstructions that alter the allocator and ready order without changing the retail frame

evidence.summary: Four simultaneously live typed Vert pointers worsen the function to 443 words, frame 0x98, and total 358, refuting that broad reconstruction at the frame gate.

bounds.tested: one four-pointer whole-region reconstruction at fixed 2.7.2-cdk -G0
bounds.untested: staged pointers with unequal short lifetimes and source-level expression dependencies

evidence.summary: Splitting only vertex3's pointer and signed-y lifetimes improves the fully depinned control from total 55 to 33 while retaining 430 words and the exact 0x80 frame. It aligns the index/pointer/field-load region but leaves global s4/s5 order, xy1 colouring, and four scheduling indels; it supports a lifetime mechanism without proving original source. The measured allocator trace identifies vertex-base pseudo 88 at priority 6846 ahead of cell-pointer pseudo 355 at 6428, with no relevant preference.

The predicted embedded height, vertex-1 split, cell-source, control-flow, and nearby reuse spellings do not repair the 33-point v20 residue. Several are byte-neutral while broader merges worsen length, frame, colouring, or scheduling. CDK remains better than the tested 2.8 cells.

bounds.tested: v20 allocator tracing; signed/direct/embedded height forms; vertex-1 split and signedness forms; bias/height reuse; typed and explicit cell forms; inner-loop control form; and 2.8.0/2.8.1 lineage checks
bounds.untested: an evidence-backed ordinary lifetime or preference that crosses the measured 6846/6428 threshold while preserving the exact post-terrain region, followed by the four potentially co-adapted sched2 indels

next_experiment.action: Starting from zero-pin v20, recover and test one evidence-backed ordinary lifetime, reuse, or preference that can lower the vertex-base priority below 6428, raise the cell-pointer priority above 6846, or otherwise make the cell pointer precede the vertex base; preserve the exact post-terrain region, then remeasure the four local sched2 indels under the corrected hard-register assignment.
next_experiment.measurement: At fixed 2.7.2-cdk -G0, capture allocator refs, live length, calls crossed, priority, global order, preferences, assigned s4/s5 roles, exact bytes, 430-word length, 0x80 frame, words 104-172, and the already exact words 295-429.
next_experiment.success_criterion: The natural source relationship gives the cell pointer s4 and vertex base s5 through the measured allocator mechanism without perturbing words 295-429, length, or frame; subsequent scheduling analysis reduces or explains the four indels without pins.
next_experiment.failure_criterion: The candidate does not cross the measured allocator threshold or changes the exact post-terrain region, frame, or length; record only that source family as a bounded negative and keep the case unresolved.
next_experiment.bounds: One small source-lifetime/preference family justified by owner or sibling evidence on hash-recorded v20 at fixed CDK; do not repeat the completed height, vertex-1, cell-loop, or broad compiler-cell forms.

cases.title: Empty asm effect on GCC delay-branch reorganization

claim.summary: GCC dbr/reorg ownership is proven with genuine and independent controls, and a literal-address diagnostic proves how to retain the nop, but that diagnostic is semantically unacceptable and no honest C repair is exact.

identity.value: SLUS translation-unit row w_80041CBC anchored by func_80041CBC at 0x80041CBC, 3880 retail bytes

causal.question: Does the original 16-byte frame-sync object have an authentic update/read relationship that keeps the symbolic HIGH out of GCC's branch delay SEQUENCE, or does this site expose a delayed-branch candidate-selection difference in the recovered compiler?
causal.prediction: A real cross-field dependency recovered from the defining object context will retain symbolic HI16/LO16 relocations and all 91 retail instructions while keeping HIGH out of the delay SEQUENCE; if no such relationship exists, a pass-level comparison should identify a site-specific recovered-versus-rebuilt 2.8.1 selection difference rather than a global assembler rule.

evidence.summary: Six local symbolic/control-flow reconstructions and a volatile symbolic byte read all compile like the pinless source at 121/122, total 26. Full symbolic and grouped-object reconstructions are also non-exact across named stock cells.

bounds.tested: six local branch/control shapes, volatile symbolic read, full symbolic source, grouped page-base source, and nine named stock cells
bounds.untested: a richer authentic update/read relationship within the 16-byte object and a site-specific recovered-versus-rebuilt delayed-branch implementation difference

evidence.summary: The empty asm creates an output dependency before GCC's delayed-branch pass. Without it, .dbr contains a branch/HIGH SEQUENCE and GCC emits the filled slot in noreorder mode before either assembler stage.

An isolated fallthrough-head control and compatible genuine GCC/ASPSX reproduce the same branch choice. Fifteen exact SLUS controls legitimately fill a delay slot with symbolic HIGH, rejecting a global assembler suppression rule.

A hardcoded absolute byte read is linked-byte exact because its multiword macro cannot fill one delay slot, proving the mechanism. It is rejected as a repair because it loses symbolic relocations, embeds the PS1 address, and harms port semantics.

The three value-lifetime probes and two authentic 16-byte declaration spellings are complete negatives. Each reuse probe still places branch and symbolic HIGH in one .dbr delay SEQUENCE; the array and struct context forms remain 121/122 at total 26.

bounds.tested: reuse_zero, frame_ticks reuse, sync_flags reuse, authentic 16-byte array extent, and authentic 16-byte fielded struct at fixed 2.8.1 -G0 with raw .greg/.dbr and linked scoring
bounds.untested: the defining TU/linker declaration plus an authentic cross-field update/read relationship, and a pass-source comparison for a site-specific compiler candidate-selection difference

next_experiment.action: Trace the defining TU/linker declaration and original update/read sequence for the 16-byte frame-sync object, then reproduce only an authentic cross-field dependency at this tail. If provenance supplies no such relationship, compare the recovered GCC/SN cc1 delayed-branch candidate selection with the rebuilt 2.8.1 pass at this site.
next_experiment.measurement: Record declaration and same-image provenance, source-level dependency, raw .greg and .dbr state, delay-SEQUENCE membership, symbolic relocations, runtime instruction count, and all 91 linked retail instructions; for the fallback, record the exact pass-source decision and divergent state.
next_experiment.success_criterion: An authentic source relationship keeps HIGH out of the delay SEQUENCE, preserves relocations and port behavior, adds no runtime instruction, and matches all 91 instructions; alternatively, pass evidence demonstrates the precise site-specific compiler selection difference.
next_experiment.failure_criterion: No authentic relationship changes the sequence and no pass-level difference is demonstrated; retain unresolved status, because this bounded failure is not an architecture or instruction-set impossibility.
next_experiment.bounds: One provenance-led reconstruction from same-image/linker evidence for the 16-byte object, followed if needed by one focused recovered-versus-rebuilt delayed-branch pass comparison; do not repeat the completed reuse or declaration-spelling probes.
